Iterated Elimination of Strictly Dominated Strategies

Watch dominated strategies get deleted one by one. Push the round slider to eliminate them in order. If a strategy always does worse than another one, no rational player uses it. Delete it and the table shrinks. In the smaller table, another bad strategy shows up. In this scene C, M, and D vanish in turn until only U remains. For example, say a 🏪 shop sells three kinds of 🍬 candy. One kind is always smaller and less tasty than another kind. Nobody ever picks it, so it can leave the shelf. Once it is gone, another always-worse candy stands out. Deleting step by step leaves the final choice.

Examples & Exercises

Run iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies for three rounds in the 3×33 \times 33×3 game, identifying what is removed and why each round.

LCRU(4,3)(5,1)(6,2)M(2,1)(8,4)(3,6)D(3,0)(9,6)(2,8)\begin{matrix} & L & C & R \\ U & (4,3) & (5,1) & (6,2) \\ M & (2,1) & (8,4) & (3,6) \\ D & (3,0) & (9,6) & (2,8) \end{matrix}UMD​L(4,3)(2,1)(3,0)​C(5,1)(8,4)(9,6)​R(6,2)(3,6)(2,8)​
Show proof
  1. Round 1: comparing player 2's payoffs, column CCC (1,4,6)(1,4,6)(1,4,6) vs column RRR (2,6,8)(2,6,8)(2,6,8) — RRR is larger in every row, so RRR strictly dominates CCC. Remove CCC.
  2. Round 2 (against {L,R}\{L,R\}{L,R}): player 1's row MMM (2,3)(2,3)(2,3) vs row UUU (4,6)(4,6)(4,6) — UUU strictly dominates. Remove MMM. Round 3: row DDD (3,2)(3,2)(3,2) vs row UUU (4,6)(4,6)(4,6) — UUU strictly dominates again. Remove DDD.
  3. Only UUU survives for player 1. Against UUU, player 2 prefers LLL (payoff 333) over RRR (payoff 222). Final outcome (U,L)=(4,3)(U, L) = (4, 3)(U,L)=(4,3) — also a Nash equilibrium (unilateral deviation loses).

Prove that iterated elimination of strictly dominated strategies never eliminates a Nash equilibrium.

If a Nash equilibrium s∗s^*s∗ used a strictly dominated si∗s_i^*si∗​, deviating to si′s_i'si′​ would strictly raise the payoff against s−i∗s_{-i}^*s−i∗​ — contradicting equilibrium.
  2. So no first-round elimination can remove part of a Nash equilibrium. The same argument applies inside the reduced game, so by induction every round preserves all Nash equilibria: the IEDS survivor set always contains every Nash equilibrium.
